questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles messages that cannot be processed (dead-lettering and retries)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A message arrives whose body is valid JSON but contains Amount = 0. What happens to it?
choices: It is abandoned and retried until the queue's MaxDeliveryCount is reached, then dead-lettered by the broker
It is completed and ignored, because the ledger is never called
It is dead-lettered immediately with reason InvalidPayload and a description, without calling the ledger
It is passed to the ledger, which is expected to throw PaymentRejectedException

questions.prompt: The ledger throws an HttpRequestException because the core banking API is down. What does the consumer do with the message?
choices: Abandons it so it becomes available again, and relies on the broker to dead-letter it only after MaxDeliveryCount deliveries
Completes it so the queue does not back up, and logs the warning
Lets the exception escape the handler so the processor completes the message automatically

questions.prompt: In DeadLetterRequeuer, why is receiver.CompleteMessageAsync called after sender.SendMessageAsync rather than before?
choices: So that a crash between the two calls can produce a duplicate on the main queue but never lose the message
So that the broker can detect the duplicate and drop the original automatically
Because a message in the dead-letter sub-queue cannot be completed until its copy has been consumed
Because completing first would reset DeliveryCount on the copy
